summary: PR #4887 (CASSANDRA-21113, base cassandra-4.0) changes PasswordObfuscator so that the password is CQL-escaped (single quote doubled) and passed through Pattern.quote() before the regex replace. This fixes the two reported failures: special regex characters ($, +, ?, etc.) that leaked the password into audit logs, and the \E sequence that threw PatternSyntaxException. It adds a CHANGES.txt entry under the 4.0.21 section and a test class with a \E test and a per-character sweep over printable ASCII. Against the ticket, the patch covers both the regex-character leak and the \E exception, and nothing outside that scope is changed, so spec_conformance is full. It is a bug fix that is minimal and suitable for a 4.0 patch release. Security surface touched: password masking in audit and DCL log output. The change tightens masking and introduces no new exposure, so no security findings. Ticket was used as the contract. Nothing in the PR modifies .claude/, AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, and no review-steering text was found beyond the standard PR template. Remaining risk is low: the escaping only handles the single-quote CQL rule, which is the only escape a CQL string literal needs.

findings.rule: Cassandra code style: needless visibility on test-local constants
findings.problem: ASCII_START and ASCII_END are declared public static final in a test class where they are only used inside the class. The public modifier adds nothing.
findings.fix: Make them private static final (or inline them in the loop).
